title: Making a hand-painted 2D beat ’em up with AI — struggling with character animation. Any advice?
author: El_nino_leone
selftext:
​

Hey everyone!

I'm working on an indie 2D beat ’em up inspired by classic arcade brawlers like *Streets of Rage*, but set in Italy.

I'm aiming for a detailed, hand-painted comic-book aesthetic rather than traditional pixel art. I'm using generative AI to help create the character illustrations, while **Godot** handles the game and animations.

My current workflow involves **ChatGPT, AI image generation, ElevenLabs Flows, and Godot**, with Codex helping with implementation.

My biggest challenge so far has been **maintaining character consistency across animation frames**.

I've been experimenting with individually generated walking poses based on traditional animation references. I started with a twelve-frame walking cycle, then tested six-, eight-, ten- and twelve-frame versions in Godot.

Eight frames looked the most promising, but I'm still struggling with:

\- Keeping character proportions, facial features, clothing and art style consistent.

\- Maintaining correct anatomy and leg positions between frames.

\- Getting natural weight transfer and foot contact.

\- Making the animation loop smoothly without foot sliding or awkward transitions.

I'm now looking into **ElevenLabs Flows** to build a more consistent workflow, ideally producing both individual sprites and complete animation previews.

I'm relatively new to game development and animation, and I'm trying to learn how professionals approach this rather than simply generating images and hoping they work together.

**For those experienced with 2D animation or AI-assisted game development:**

Would you recommend generating individual frames, using skeletal animation, working in a dedicated animation tool, or combining different approaches?

Are there any specific tools or techniques that work particularly well for detailed, hand-painted characters?

I'd especially appreciate hearing from anyone who has experimented with AI-generated animation for games, including what hasn't worked.

Thanks!

comments.author: stolenyourgf
comments.body: what helped me most was locking one "model sheet" frame and only redoing legs and arms per frame, head and torso pasted from the same source every time. the foot sliding is usually on the game side tho, match move speed to how far the planted foot travels per frame. 8 frames is plenty for a brawler walk

comments.author: Sloptrawler
comments.body:
What works for me is to generate models with posable limbs first then use them as inputs to an animation sheet where it generates them all at once (like 8 frames.) I then say "turn this pose sheet into this character" (then supply the pose and your character sheet as images.)  
There are local AI models you can run that are just for dances or movement, but you may have the best luck just making the poses you want in something like blender then then applying your character overtop.
